title: RF effects in components
blurb: Explain skin effect, parasitic reactance, electrical length, and the difference between real and reactive power.

E5D01.why: At RF the current flows near the surface, so less conductor carries it and **resistance increases with frequency**.
E5D01.trap: Electron mobility and temperature coefficients are unrelated to skin effect.

E5D02.why: Leads act as small inductors: their reactance (2πfL) grows with frequency. Short leads **minimise inductive reactance** at VHF and up.

E5D03.why: Reactive power means voltage and current are **90° out of phase**.
E5D03.trap: In phase is real power; 45° is a mix of both.

E5D04.why: A longer connection is a bigger fraction of a short wavelength, so **phase shift** along it grows. Short connections reduce it.

E5D05.why: An electrolytic capacitor's construction adds series **inductance**, so at RF it stops acting like a capacitor.
E5D05.trap: Skin effect is a resistance issue, not what defeats electrolytics.

E5D06.why: Neighbouring turns act as a small capacitor across the inductor: **inter-turn capacitance** gives it a self-resonance.

E5D07.why: Self-resonance occurs where the part's **nominal and parasitic reactance** are equal and opposite.
E5D07.trap: Resistance does not cause resonance. It takes the part's own reactance plus an opposite parasitic one.

E5D08.why: At RF, current crowds to the surface of the conductors, so **skin effect** is the main loss in film capacitors.
E5D08.trap: Dielectric loss exists, but skin effect is the primary RF loss in film capacitors.

E5D09.why: Ideal L and C store energy in magnetic or electric fields and return it, so **no power is dissipated**.
E5D09.trap: Heat comes from resistance, not from reactance.

E5D10.why: A thicker conductor has a greater **electrical length** than a thinner one of the same physical length.

E5D11.why: Only R dissipates: P = I² × R = 1² × 100 = **100 W**. The 141.4 is apparent power (VA).

E5D12.why: Reactive power is **wattless, nonproductive power**: energy shuttled in and out of L and C.
E5D12.trap: It is not consumed in the parts' wire resistance; that is real loss.
